text:
jess: heads-up: Enterprise Acme reported invoice tokens > dashboard tokens after they flipped on continuous-batching yesterday. #urgent
ryan_ops: can you paste request ids or sample invoice?
jess: invoice id INV-2026-3312 — customer says dashboard showed ~1.2M tokens for month, invoice billed 1.8M. They narrowed it to a 3-day window after rolling cont-batcher.
maria: Is this the same continuous-batcher rollout we did for dedicated-pool-2? any config changes like prefetch_enabled=true or prefix_warmup=on?
jess: yes prefetch=true, prefix_warmup=sampled. Their app attaches a big user-profile prompt prefix per request.
raj: likely double-counting from prefetched prefixes at the metering boundary. Need metering.v2 logs + the request_id for a concrete repro.
jess: I repro'd locally with a single request that still shows spike. sample curl to reproduce quickly:```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"xlarge-v2","prompt":"<profile data>...","continuous_batch":true,"prefetch":true}'```
billing-eng: reading this — quick note: invoices are generated from meter events recorded at ingress after the batcher expands examples. The dashboard shows a deduped view (post-cache/hot-path) for convenience. That mismatch explains some deltas when prefetch materializes tokens across many examples.
ryan_ops: can you grab a few lines from metering for one of those request_ids? grep for request_id/expanded fields and paste here (truncate any PII).
jess: pasted 3 lines from metering for req=abc123:```[metering.v2] req=abc123 expanded=12 served=180 billed=180 cache_hit=false prefix_prefetch=true``` ```[cache] req=abc123 hit=false store_key=usr-42-prefix len=512``` ```[batcher] req=abc123 batch_size=12 continuous=true```
raj: That expanded=12 means continuous-batcher replicated the prefix across 12 examples; metering records all served tokens when the batch expands. Later, once the prefix is cached, subsequent requests become cache_hit=true and dashboard dedupes them — invoice already captured the initial expansion.
billing-eng: We can approach this two ways: short term, run a reconciliation that computes "deduped_served" by collapsing prefix tokens within a sliding window; long term, emit a prefetch marker and avoid counting ephemeral prefetch tokens in invoice. Both need product/finance review.
maria: Customer wants immediate credit if the delta >10%. Can billing produce a reconciled breakdown and proposed credit amount?
billing-eng: I'll run reconciliation for INV-2026-3312 and return a breakdown (grouped by prefetched_prefix vs interactive tokens). ETA ~4h. If confirmed, propose a one-off credit for the delta attributable to prefetch materialization — cc: @finance.
jess: :thumbsup: I will update the customer ticket with ETA and the temporary workaround: either 1) reduce prefix size, or 2) disable prefetch/continuous-batching for that workload while we reconcile.
ingest-bot: logs-upload complete -> https://logs.redwood.ai/ingest/abc123 (contains metering.v2 captures + batcher traces)
raj: Follow-up (engineering): long-term fix options: 1) meter post-cache dedupe (meter only after KV cache lookup), 2) mark prefetch-materialization events with a separate meter tag so billing can exclude them, or 3) change batcher to emit a single logical served event for shared prefix. I'll open an RFC and include perf/latency tradeoffs.
jess: thanks all. I'll log internal KB entry: "Note: continuous-batcher + prefetch can temporarily inflate billed tokens vs dashboard until cache convergence. Support steps: collect request_ids, metering.v2 lines, and provide this reconciliation ETA to customer."
